answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils expensive: a new agent only gains influence when established peers stake a deposit to vouch for it, like a reef built from many anchored commitments. If the newcomer misbehaves, slashing drains those bonds, so vouchers risk real capital. An attacker spinning up a dune of fake identities must self-fund every bond; the rising tide of forfeited stake per detected fake makes mass fabrication cost more than any gains.
